title: Polity Lec 3
summary: Part I (Art. 1-4): Art. 1 - India as a Union of States; Art. 2 - admission/establishment of new states; Art. 3 - formation of new states and alteration of areas, boundaries or names; Art. 4 - such laws pass by simple majority and are not amendments under Art. 368.
A bill under Art. 3 needs the President's recommendation; the views of the state legislature are sought but are not binding; the time-limit provision came with the 5th Amendment (1955).
First Schedule - names and territories of states and UTs; Fourth Schedule - allocation of Rajya Sabha seats (in proportion to population; Uttar Pradesh 31, Sikkim 1).
Union Territories: Dadra and Nagar Haveli - 10th, Goa, Daman and Diu - 12th, Puducherry - 14th Amendment; Goa became a state in 1987; Operation Vijay 1961; Vasco da Gama arrived in 1498.
Sikkim: 35th Amendment 1974 (associate state, Art. 2A), 36th Amendment 1975 (full-fledged state).

First state formed on a linguistic basis: Andhra (1953, Potti Sriramulu); Fazl Ali Commission (Fazl Ali, H.N. Kunzru, K.M. Panikkar); States Reorganisation Act 1956 - 14 states, 6 UTs; Dhar Commission and JVP Committee 1948.
Berubari case 1960: acquiring territory by simple majority, ceding territory needs a constitutional amendment (9th Amendment); Bangladesh Land Boundary Agreement - 100th Amendment.
Key amendments: 97th - cooperative societies, 101st - GST, 102nd - NCBC, 103rd - 10% EWS quota, 104th - end of Anglo-Indian nomination, 106th - Nari Shakti Vandan (33%).
Art. 371 sequence: 371 Maharashtra-Gujarat; 371A-J respectively Nagaland, Assam, Manipur, Andhra Pradesh, Andhra university, Sikkim, Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh, Goa, Karnataka.

Part II (Art. 5-11) Citizenship: Art. 6 cut-off 19 July 1948, Art. 7 cut-off 1 March 1947, Art. 8 persons of Indian origin abroad, Art. 9 voluntary foreign citizenship, Art. 10 continuance, Art. 11 Parliament's power to legislate.

Citizenship Act 1955: 5 modes of acquisition (birth, descent, registration, naturalisation, incorporation of territory); 3 modes of loss (renunciation, termination, deprivation); birth rules tightened in 1987 and 2003; single citizenship (from Britain).

Gupta period: Chandragupta I - Maharajadhiraja; Samudragupta - Prayag Prashasti (Harishena), 'Napoleon of India', veena coins; Chandragupta II - Vikramaditya; officials: Sandhivigrahika, Kumaramatya, Mahadandanayaka, Uparika, Ayukta.
Administration: Bhukti (province) > Vishaya (Vishayapati) > Vithi > Grama (Gramika); taxes: Bhaga, Uparikara, Vishti, Halivakara, Hiranya.

Nalanda - Kumaragupta I; Vikramashila - Dharmapala; Odantapuri - Gopala. Chalukyas: Badami caves, Aihole (Durga temple), Pattadakal (Virupaksha); Rashtrakuta founder Dantidurga, Kailasa temple at Ellora - Krishna I.

Pallavas: Mahendravarman I - rock-cut temples, Narasimhavarman I - Pancha Rathas, Narasimhavarman II - Kailasanatha and Shore Temple; Harshavardhana - Pushyabhuti dynasty, Thanesar; Aihole inscription (Ravikirti).

mcqs.q: In Lecture 3, Part I of the Constitution deals with which subject?
mcqs.e: Part I (Art. 1-4) - Union and its territory; Part II (Art. 5-11) - Citizenship.

mcqs.q: Which Articles fall under Part I of the Constitution?
mcqs.e: Part I contains four Articles in all.

mcqs.q: Which Article empowers Parliament to admit or establish new states?
mcqs.e: Art. 2 - admission/establishment of new states (bringing outside territory into India).

mcqs.q: Formation of a new state from an existing one, altering its area, boundaries or name is done under which Article?
mcqs.e: Art. 3 deals with reorganisation of existing states (formation, area, boundary, name).

mcqs.q: Which Article is used to admit into India a territory that is not yet part of India?
mcqs.e: Acquiring territory from outside falls under Art. 2.

mcqs.q: Bifurcation of a state or merger of two states is done under which Article?
mcqs.e: Bifurcation and merger of states are done under Art. 3.

mcqs.q: When were Uttarakhand, Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand formed?
mcqs.e: All three were carved out in 2000 from Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Bihar respectively.

mcqs.q: Chhattisgarh was carved out of which state?
mcqs.e: Chhattisgarh - from MP; Uttarakhand - from UP; Jharkhand - from Bihar.

mcqs.q: Jharkhand was carved out of which state?
mcqs.e: Jharkhand was formed from Bihar on 15 November 2000.

mcqs.q: When was the state of Telangana formed?
mcqs.e: Telangana was carved out of Andhra Pradesh as India's 29th state.

mcqs.q: What majority is required for laws made under Articles 2 and 3?
o: Special majority plus ratification by half the states
mcqs.e: Under Art. 4 such laws are not Art. 368 amendments; a simple majority suffices.

mcqs.q: What does a simple majority mean?
o: More than half of the members present and voting
mcqs.e: Simple majority = more than 50% of members present and voting.

mcqs.q: According to Article 4, laws made under Art. 2 or 3 are exempt from which procedure?
mcqs.e: Such laws are exempt from the Art. 368 procedure.

mcqs.q: Which two procedures (involving special majority) are followed under Article 368?
o: Special majority; and special majority plus ratification by at least half the states
mcqs.e: That is why Art. 2/3 laws do not need the Art. 368 procedure.

mcqs.q: Whose prior recommendation is required before introducing a bill under Article 3?
mcqs.e: Such a bill can be introduced in Parliament only on the President's recommendation.

mcqs.q: Why does the President refer an Article 3 bill to the concerned state legislature?
mcqs.e: The state's views are not binding on Parliament.

mcqs.q: In Article 3 matters, how binding are the views of the state legislature on Parliament?
mcqs.e: Parliament is not bound to accept the state's views.

mcqs.q: Which amendment empowered the President to fix a time limit for the state legislature to express its views?
mcqs.e: Since the 5th Amendment (1955) the President can prescribe the time limit.

mcqs.q: The names and territories of the states are listed in which Schedule of the Constitution?
mcqs.e: First Schedule - names and territories of states and Union Territories.

mcqs.q: Allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha is given in which Schedule?
mcqs.e: Fourth Schedule - allocation of Rajya Sabha seats to states/UTs.

mcqs.q: On what basis are Rajya Sabha seats allocated?
mcqs.e: More populous states get more seats.

mcqs.q: By what system are Rajya Sabha members elected?
o: Indirect election, proportional representation by single transferable vote
mcqs.e: Rajya Sabha members are elected by MLAs through STV.

mcqs.q: How many Rajya Sabha seats does Uttar Pradesh have?
mcqs.e: UP has 31 seats (the most); Sikkim has only 1.

mcqs.q: According to Article 4, the First and Fourth Schedules can be changed by what majority?
mcqs.e: Because of Art. 4, these Schedules can be changed by simple majority.

mcqs.q: Emergency provisions are contained in which Part of the Constitution?
mcqs.e: Part XVIII (Art. 352-360) - Emergency.

mcqs.q: Fundamental Rights are contained in which Part of the Constitution?
mcqs.e: Part III - Articles 12 to 35.

mcqs.q: Goa, Daman and Diu were made a Union Territory by which amendment?
mcqs.e: The 12th Amendment (1962) made Goa, Daman and Diu a UT after their liberation in 1961.

mcqs.q: Dadra and Nagar Haveli was made a UT by which amendment?
mcqs.e: 10th Amendment (1961).

mcqs.q: By which amendment was Puducherry incorporated into India as a Union Territory?
mcqs.e: Puducherry was earlier under French control.

mcqs.q: In which year did Goa get full statehood?
mcqs.e: Goa became the 25th state in 1987 (Goa, Daman and Diu Reorganisation Act; 56th Amendment).

mcqs.q: Goa, Daman and Diu became a UT by the 12th Amendment. Which amendment, two numbers earlier, made Dadra and Nagar Haveli a UT?
mcqs.e: 12 - 2 = 10 (Dadra and Nagar Haveli); 12 + 2 = 14 (Puducherry).

mcqs.q: Puducherry was under the control of which European power?
mcqs.e: Puducherry was French; Goa, Daman, Diu and Dadra were Portuguese.

mcqs.q: Goa, Daman and Diu and Dadra and Nagar Haveli were under which European power?
mcqs.e: The Portuguese were the first to arrive and the last to leave.

mcqs.q: When did Vasco da Gama reach India (Calicut)?
mcqs.e: The Portuguese arrived in 1498.

mcqs.q: Which military operation in 1961 ended Portuguese rule in Goa?
mcqs.e: Operation Vijay (December 1961) brought Goa, Daman and Diu into India.

mcqs.q: Which uniform civil code is in force in Goa?
mcqs.e: Goa follows the Portuguese-era civil code, not one framed by independent India.

mcqs.q: The Uniform Civil Code is mentioned in which Article?
mcqs.e: Art. 44 (DPSP) - Uniform Civil Code.

mcqs.q: Which was the first state to implement a UCC after independence (as of November 2025)?
mcqs.e: Uttarakhand implemented its UCC in January 2025 (memory aid: U for UCC, U for Uttarakhand).

mcqs.q: What does Article 1 call India?
mcqs.e: 'India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States.'

mcqs.q: According to Dr. Ambedkar, why was the term 'Union of States' used?
o: The Indian Union is indestructible and states have no right to secede
mcqs.e: India is an 'indestructible Union of destructible states'.

mcqs.q: Which statement about India is correct?
mcqs.e: States can be reorganised but cannot secede from the Union.

mcqs.q: Where is the word 'Federation' used in the Constitution?
mcqs.e: The word 'federation' is not used anywhere in the Constitution.

mcqs.q: According to Article 1, what does the territory of India comprise?
o: States, Union Territories and territories that may be acquired
mcqs.e: Three categories: states, UTs and acquired territories.

mcqs.q: Article 1 indicates which aspect of India?
o: Nature of the polity (Union) and its territory
mcqs.e: It states the type of polity and its territory.

mcqs.q: The agreement on Berubari Union (West Bengal) was signed between whom?
mcqs.e: Signed in 1958 between Nehru and Pakistan PM Feroz Khan Noon.

mcqs.q: What did the Supreme Court hold in the Berubari Union case (1960)?
o: The President alone can cede territory
Territory can be ceded by simple majority
Territory can be acquired by simple majority, but ceding it requires a constitutional amendment
mcqs.e: Hence the 9th Amendment was enacted.

mcqs.q: Which amendment was required to transfer Berubari to Pakistan?
mcqs.e: 9th Constitutional Amendment, 1960.

mcqs.q: The Land Boundary Agreement (enclaves) with Bangladesh was given effect by which amendment?
mcqs.e: 100th Amendment (2015) - India transferred 111 enclaves and received 51.

mcqs.q: The 97th Amendment relates to which subject?
mcqs.e: The 97th Amendment (2011) added Part IXB.

mcqs.q: The 101st Constitutional Amendment relates to what?
mcqs.e: 101st Amendment, 2016 - GST.

mcqs.q: Which body got constitutional status through the 102nd Amendment?
mcqs.e: Art. 338B was inserted, giving NCBC constitutional status.

mcqs.q: What did the 103rd Constitutional Amendment provide?
mcqs.e: 103rd Amendment, 2019.

mcqs.q: What was done by the 104th Amendment?
o: Ended Anglo-Indian nomination and extended SC/ST reservation by 10 years
mcqs.e: 104th Amendment (2019).

mcqs.q: How many members of the Anglo-Indian community could the President nominate to the Lok Sabha?
mcqs.e: The President nominated 2 to the Lok Sabha and a Governor 1 to the Assembly.

mcqs.q: By what name is the 106th Constitutional Amendment known?
mcqs.e: 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state Assemblies.

mcqs.q: Under the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, what share of seats in the Lok Sabha and Assemblies is reserved for women?
mcqs.e: One-third (33%) reservation (106th Amendment, 2023).

mcqs.q: Article 371 (the first in the series) makes special provisions for which states?
mcqs.e: Art. 371 - Maharashtra and Gujarat.

mcqs.q: Article 371A relates to which state?
mcqs.e: 371A Nagaland, B Assam, C Manipur, D-E Andhra, F Sikkim, G Mizoram, H Arunachal, I Goa, J Karnataka.

mcqs.q: Article 371B is for which state?
mcqs.e: 371B - Assam.

mcqs.q: Article 371C is for which state?
mcqs.e: 371C - Manipur.

mcqs.q: Articles 371D and 371E respectively relate to what?
o: Andhra Pradesh/Telangana and a central university in Andhra Pradesh
mcqs.e: 371D - Andhra Pradesh/Telangana; 371E - central university in Andhra Pradesh.

mcqs.q: Article 371F is for which state?
mcqs.e: 371F - Sikkim.

mcqs.q: Article 371G is for which state?
mcqs.e: 371G - Mizoram.

mcqs.q: Article 371H is for which state?
mcqs.e: 371H - Arunachal Pradesh; 371I - Goa.

mcqs.q: Article 371J is for which state (region)?
mcqs.e: 371J - Karnataka; 371I - Goa.

mcqs.q: By which amendment did Sikkim get the status of an 'Associate State'?
mcqs.e: The 35th Amendment inserted Art. 2A.

mcqs.q: Which Article was inserted into the Constitution by the 35th Amendment?
mcqs.e: Art. 2A - Sikkim as an associate state.

mcqs.q: By which amendment did Sikkim become a full-fledged state?
mcqs.e: The 36th Amendment made Sikkim the 22nd state, ending Chogyal rule.

mcqs.q: The rule of which dynasty ended in Sikkim?
mcqs.e: The Chogyal dynasty.

mcqs.q: Which was the first state of India formed on a linguistic basis?
mcqs.e: Andhra State was carved out of Madras in 1953.

mcqs.q: Who died during a fast unto death demanding a separate Andhra state?
mcqs.e: Potti Sriramulu died during his fast in 1952.

mcqs.q: Who was the chairman of the States Reorganisation Commission (Fazl Ali Commission)?
mcqs.e: The commission was set up in 1953.

mcqs.q: Who were the other two members of the Fazl Ali Commission?
o: Hriday Nath Kunzru and K.M. Panikkar
mcqs.e: The commission had 3 members in all.

mcqs.q: When was the States Reorganisation Act passed?
mcqs.e: It abolished the Part A/B/C/D classification and created 14 states and 6 UTs.

mcqs.q: How many states and UTs were created by the States Reorganisation Act, 1956?
mcqs.e: The Part A, B, C, D classification was abolished.

mcqs.q: Which bodies (1948) recommended against forming states on a linguistic basis?
mcqs.e: Both favoured administrative convenience as the basis for states.

mcqs.q: Who were the members of the JVP Committee?
o: Jawaharlal Nehru, Vallabhbhai Patel, Pattabhi Sitaramayya
mcqs.e: J-V-P is named after these three.

mcqs.q: When were the Dhar Commission and the JVP Committee constituted?
mcqs.e: Both were set up in 1948.

mcqs.q: Part II of the Constitution deals with which subject?
mcqs.e: Part II - Articles 5 to 11.

mcqs.q: Which Articles deal with citizenship?
mcqs.e: Part II.

mcqs.q: Articles 5 to 11 deal with citizenship as on which date?
mcqs.e: Citizenship after this date is governed by the Citizenship Act, 1955.

mcqs.q: After 26 January 1950, acquisition and loss of citizenship are governed by what?
mcqs.e: Art. 5-10 are now largely spent; the 1955 Act governs.

mcqs.q: Which Article provides for citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution?
mcqs.e: Art. 5 - citizenship at commencement (domicile plus birth, parent's birth or residence).

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT a requirement for citizenship under Article 5?
mcqs.e: A passport is not a requirement for citizenship.

mcqs.q: Article 6 relates to whom?
o: Persons of Indian origin living abroad
Persons who migrated to Pakistan and returned
Certain persons who migrated to India from Pakistan
mcqs.e: Art. 6 - migrants from Pakistan.

mcqs.q: What is the cut-off date in Article 6 for persons migrating from Pakistan?
mcqs.e: Those arriving after this date needed registration.

mcqs.q: When could a person who came from Pakistan after 19 July 1948 become a citizen?
o: When registered by an officer appointed by the Government of India
mcqs.e: Registration was required.

mcqs.q: Article 7 relates to whom?
o: Persons who migrated to Pakistan and later returned to India
mcqs.e: Art. 7 - migrants to Pakistan.

mcqs.q: What is the cut-off date in Article 7?
mcqs.e: Memory aid: 'seven-seven' (Art. 7 and 1947).

mcqs.q: Article 8 relates to whom?
o: Persons of Indian origin residing outside India
mcqs.e: Art. 8 - citizenship of persons of Indian origin residing abroad.

mcqs.q: Under Article 8, where do persons of Indian origin living abroad apply for citizenship?
o: Only the Ministry of Home Affairs
Indian embassy/consulate in the country of residence
mcqs.e: Registration by the Indian diplomatic or consular representative.

mcqs.q: Which Article states that a person voluntarily acquiring foreign citizenship ceases to be an Indian citizen?
mcqs.e: Art. 9 - those voluntarily acquiring foreign citizenship are not citizens.

mcqs.q: Which Article provides for the continuance of the rights of citizenship?
mcqs.e: Art. 10 - continuance of rights of citizenship.

mcqs.q: Which Article empowers Parliament to make laws on citizenship?
mcqs.e: Art. 11 - Parliament can legislate on acquisition and termination of citizenship.

mcqs.q: Who can make laws on citizenship?
mcqs.e: Citizenship is a Union List subject.

mcqs.q: What does Article 12 define?
mcqs.e: Art. 12 (Part III) defines 'State'; Art. 36 adopts the same meaning.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT included in the definition of 'State' under Art. 12?
mcqs.e: Parliament, legislatures, governments, local and other authorities are included.

mcqs.q: What happens when an Indian citizen renounces Indian citizenship?
mcqs.e: Renunciation ends Indian citizenship; India does not allow dual citizenship.

mcqs.q: What type of citizenship does India have?
mcqs.e: Single citizenship was borrowed from the British Constitution.

mcqs.q: The provision of single citizenship was borrowed from which country's constitution?
mcqs.e: From Britain: parliamentary system, bicameralism, FPTP, prerogative writs, etc.

mcqs.q: How many modes of acquiring citizenship are there under the Citizenship Act, 1955?
mcqs.e: Birth, descent, registration, naturalisation, incorporation of territory.

mcqs.q: How many modes of losing citizenship are there under the Citizenship Act, 1955?
mcqs.e: Renunciation, termination, deprivation.

mcqs.q: What are the three modes of losing citizenship?
mcqs.e: Renunciation, Termination, Deprivation.

mcqs.q: What is the principle of 'jus soli' in citizenship by birth?
o: Citizenship based on place of birth (soil)
mcqs.e: Jus soli = right of the soil.

mcqs.q: What does 'jus sanguinis' mean?
mcqs.e: Jus sanguinis = right of blood.

mcqs.q: When did India shift from jus soli towards jus sanguinis for citizenship by birth (tightened further in 2003)?
mcqs.e: From 1987 at least one parent must be a citizen; from 2003 the other must not be an illegal migrant.

mcqs.q: After the 2003 amendment, what is required for citizenship by birth?
o: One parent Indian and the other not an illegal migrant
mcqs.e: The rule was made stricter.

mcqs.q: How can a foreigner who has lived in India for 12 years acquire Indian citizenship?
mcqs.e: The residence requirement applies to naturalisation.

mcqs.q: A child born outside India to an Indian parent acquires citizenship by which mode?
mcqs.e: Descent.

mcqs.q: For citizenship by descent, within what period must the child's birth be registered (as per the lecture)?
mcqs.e: Registration within one year of birth.

mcqs.q: Who composed the Prayag Prashasti (Allahabad Pillar Inscription)?
mcqs.e: Harishena was Samudragupta's court poet.

mcqs.q: Harishena was the court poet of which ruler?
mcqs.e: The Prayag Prashasti eulogises Samudragupta.

mcqs.q: Which title did the Gupta ruler Chandragupta I assume?
mcqs.e: He ruled c. 319-335 CE.

mcqs.q: Which Maukhari ruler also assumed the title Maharajadhiraja?
mcqs.e: The title means 'great king of kings'.

mcqs.q: Samudragupta's reign was approximately when?
mcqs.e: Samudragupta was the son of Chandragupta I.

mcqs.q: Chandragupta II's reign was approximately when?
mcqs.e: His elder brother Ramagupta is said to have ruled before him.

mcqs.q: Which title did Chandragupta II assume after defeating the Shakas?
mcqs.e: He defeated Rudrasimha III, the last Western Kshatrapa (Shaka) ruler.

mcqs.q: What was the name of Ramagupta's widow whom Chandragupta II married?
mcqs.e: Dhruvadevi; Kuberanaga was another queen of Chandragupta II.

mcqs.q: Chandragupta II's daughter Prabhavati Gupta was married into which dynasty?
mcqs.e: This marriage allied the Guptas with the Vakatakas.

mcqs.q: Who was the 'Kumaramatya' in the Gupta empire?
o: A key high-ranking official (comparable to today's IAS)
mcqs.e: Kumaramatya - an important cadre of officials.

mcqs.q: Who was the 'Sandhivigrahika'?
mcqs.e: Sandhi-vigraha = peace and war.

mcqs.q: The post of 'Mahadandanayaka' was related to what?
mcqs.e: Harishena held the posts of Sandhivigrahika, Kumaramatya and Mahadandanayaka.

mcqs.q: Who was the 'Nagara Shreshthi'?
mcqs.e: Harishena did not hold this post.

mcqs.q: In the Gupta period, the 'Ranabhandagarika' was an officer in charge of what?
mcqs.e: In charge of military stores.

mcqs.q: Who was the 'Pilupati'?
mcqs.e: Pilu = elephant.

mcqs.q: What was the function of the 'Mahapratihara'?
mcqs.e: Acted as head of the palace guard.

mcqs.q: In Gupta administration, what did 'Bhukti' mean?
mcqs.e: Bhukti = province, headed by the Uparika.

mcqs.q: In the Gupta period, what was a 'Vishaya' and who headed it?
mcqs.e: Bhukti > Vishaya > Vithi > Grama (Gramika).

mcqs.q: What was the village headman called in the Gupta period?
mcqs.e: Gramika - village headman; Mahattara - village elder.

mcqs.q: In the Gupta period, who was the provincial governor, also handling judicial matters?
mcqs.e: The Uparika was the provincial governor.

mcqs.q: In the Gupta period, which senior officials were responsible for revenue collection?
mcqs.e: The main duty of the Ayuktas was revenue collection.

mcqs.q: Who was the 'Prathama Kulika'?
mcqs.e: Kulika = artisan.

mcqs.q: Who was the 'Prathama Kayastha'?
mcqs.e: The official who kept written records.

mcqs.q: In the Gupta period, the terms 'Chata and Bhata' referred to whom?
mcqs.e: Chata - regular troops; Bhata - irregular/temporary troops.

mcqs.q: In the Gupta period, land grants were generally given to whom?
mcqs.e: Agrahara lands were also administered by Brahmins.

mcqs.q: What was the capital of the Maitraka dynasty?
mcqs.e: The Maitrakas were Gupta feudatories who later became powerful.

mcqs.q: Who issued the earliest Maitraka land grant (502 CE)?
mcqs.e: Dronasimha; later Dhruvasena and Dharapatta.

mcqs.q: Who founded Nalanda University?
mcqs.e: It was destroyed by Bakhtiyar Khalji.

mcqs.q: Who destroyed Nalanda University?
mcqs.e: At the end of the 12th century.

mcqs.q: Who founded Vikramashila University?
mcqs.e: The Pala ruler Dharmapala.

mcqs.q: Who built Odantapuri University?
mcqs.e: Gopala.

mcqs.q: What was the capital of the Pallava dynasty?
mcqs.e: Pallavas - Kanchi.

mcqs.q: Who is considered the founder of the Pallava dynasty (as per the lecture)?
mcqs.e: Traditionally Simhavishnu.

mcqs.q: Who founded the Eastern Chalukya dynasty and what was its capital?
mcqs.e: Eastern Chalukyas - Vengi.

mcqs.q: Who founded the Chalukya dynasty of Badami (Vatapi)?
mcqs.e: The Badami caves were built by the Chalukyas.

mcqs.q: Who composed the Aihole inscription?
mcqs.e: For Pulakeshin II; it describes his victory over Harsha on the Narmada.

mcqs.q: Who defeated Harshavardhana on the banks of the Narmada?
mcqs.e: Known from the Aihole inscription.

mcqs.q: Which Pallava ruler defeated Pulakeshin II?
mcqs.e: Pulakeshin defeated Mahendravarman I; his son Narasimhavarman I then defeated Pulakeshin.

mcqs.q: Who founded the Rashtrakuta dynasty by defeating the Chalukyas of Badami?
mcqs.e: Dantidurga defeated Kirtivarman II.

mcqs.q: Who built the Kailasa temple (Cave 16) at Ellora?
mcqs.e: The Kailasanatha temple at Kanchi was built by Narasimhavarman II.

mcqs.q: Who built the Kailasanatha temple at Kanchi and the Shore Temple?
mcqs.e: Pallava art.

mcqs.q: Which Pallava ruler built the Pancha Rathas (Mahabalipuram)?
mcqs.e: Narasimhavarman I was called 'Mamalla'.

mcqs.q: Which Pallava ruler started the construction of rock-cut temples?
mcqs.e: Mainly carved out of granite.

mcqs.q: Which statement about the Durga temple at Aihole is correct?
o: It is a temple of goddess Durga
'Durg' here means fort; it is not linked to goddess Durga
It was built by the Pallavas
mcqs.e: Aihole is called the 'cradle of Indian temple architecture'.

mcqs.q: Who built the Virupaksha temple at Pattadakal?
mcqs.e: A Chalukya construction.

mcqs.q: Which of the following temples is NOT part of the Pattadakal group?
mcqs.e: The Durga temple is at Aihole.

mcqs.q: Where is the other Virupaksha temple, located in the former capital of Vijayanagara?
mcqs.e: Hampi was the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire.

mcqs.q: What was the main source of revenue of the Pallavas?
mcqs.e: Land tax was 1/6 of the total produce.

mcqs.q: What was the tax called 'Bhaga'?
o: 1/6 of the produce paid by cultivators
mcqs.e: Bhaga = the king's share.

mcqs.q: What kind of tax was 'Uparikara'?
mcqs.e: A tax over and above the regular tax.

mcqs.q: What was 'Vishti'?
mcqs.e: Vishti = forced labour (like vetti in Chola times).

mcqs.q: On what was 'Halivakara' levied?
mcqs.e: Paid by those who owned a plough.

mcqs.q: What was the 'Hiranya' tax?
mcqs.e: Hiranya (gold) - tax collected in cash.

mcqs.q: What affected Indo-Byzantine trade?
o: Byzantium learning the technique of silk production
mcqs.e: Byzantium earlier imported silk from India/China.

mcqs.q: Yajnavarman, Shardulavarman and Anantavarman were rulers of which dynasty?
mcqs.e: The Maukharis later ruled from Kannauj.

mcqs.q: What is another name of the Vardhana dynasty?
mcqs.e: Capital Thanesar (Haryana), later Kannauj.

mcqs.q: Who was the first notable king of the Pushyabhuti dynasty (580-605 CE)?
mcqs.e: His sons: Rajyavardhana (elder) and Harshavardhana (younger).

mcqs.q: Harshavardhana belonged to which dynasty/region?
mcqs.e: Capital Thanesar, later Kannauj.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT among the epigraphic sources of Harsha?
mcqs.e: Banskhera, Madhuban and the Nalanda seals relate to Harsha.

mcqs.q: What did the 'Chaturangini' army consist of, and which arm later gained importance?
mcqs.e: Chariots declined in importance while cavalry rose.

mcqs.q: Who called Samudragupta the 'Napoleon of India'?
mcqs.e: Smith described him as an undefeated warrior.

mcqs.q: On his coins, Samudragupta is shown playing which instrument?
mcqs.e: Lyrist (veena-player) type coins.

mcqs.q: In the Chola/Pallava period, what was the 'Ur'?
mcqs.e: The 'Sabha' was the assembly of learned Brahmins.

mcqs.q: The local assembly of a Brahmadeya village was managed mainly by which class?
mcqs.e: Brahmadeya = land granted to Brahmins.

mcqs.q: The term 'Tadaga' was used for what?
mcqs.e: Kshetra = agricultural land; Prapa = drinking-water shed.

mcqs.q: Tirabhukti corresponds to which present-day region?
mcqs.e: Jejakabhukti = Bundelkhand.

mcqs.q: The Jejakabhukti region corresponds to which present-day area?
mcqs.e: Bundelkhand in Madhya Pradesh/Uttar Pradesh.

mcqs.q: In the Milindapanho, whose questions are put to Nagasena?
mcqs.e: Milinda was one of the greatest Indo-Greek rulers.

mcqs.q: Who wrote the Arthashastra?
o: Kautilya (in the time of Chandragupta Maurya)
mcqs.e: A work of the Mauryan period.

mcqs.q: Which temple style did the Chalukyas develop?
mcqs.e: Chalukya temples are in the Vesara (Karnata Dravida) style.

mcqs.q: What type are the famous caves of Badami?
mcqs.e: Built by the Chalukyas of Badami (Karnataka).
